description_full: FTI Consulting, Inc. provides business advisory services to manage change, mitigate risk, and resolve disputes worldwide. The company operates through Corporate Finance; Forensic and Litigation Consulting; Economic Consulting; and Technology, and Strategic Communications segments. The Corporate Finance segment provides transactions, transformation and turnaround, and restructuring services. The Forensic and Litigation Consulting segment offers construction, projects and assets and environmental solutions, data and analytics, dispute advisory services, healthcare risk management and advisory, and risk and investigations, which include cybersecurity and financial services-related offerings. The Economic Consulting segment provides antitrust and competition economics, financial economics, and international arbitration services. The Technology segment offers blockchain and digital assets, information governance, privacy and security, investigations, litigation, M&A, and antitrust and competition services. The Strategic Communications segment provides corporate reputation, financial communications, and public affairs services. It serves aerospace and defense, airlines and aviation, blockchain and digital assets, chemicals, construction and environmental solutions, energy, financial services, food and agribusiness, healthcare and life sciences, hospitality, gaming and leisure, automotive and industrial, insurance, mining, power and products, renewable and energy transition, professional services, public sector and government contracts, real estate, retail and consumer products, telecom, media and technology, and transportation and logistics sectors. The company was incorporated in 1982 and is headquartered in Washington, the District of Columbia.

financial_summary: FTI Consulting, Inc. is a mid-cap industrials business with a $5.5B market cap on $3.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +8% over the past three years and +8% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 17% against a 7% cost of capital, a 10-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 32%.

The business throws off $94M in free cash flow — roughly 2 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.56×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.2× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage of 18× is fortress-like.
Management returns a meaningful 15.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 2.2% of the shares.

Tariff and trade-policy exposure — industrial exporters sit squarely in the crosshairs of protectionist policy, and retaliatory tariffs can close markets without warning.

prof: ROIC of 17% clears the cost of capital of 7.0% by 10pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.53).

hlth: Leverage is conservative at 0.2x net debt to EBITDA ($265.1M of cash against $365.0M of debt), with interest covered 18.2x.
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 4.3, in the safe zone).

growth: Revenue has compounded at 7.7% over 3 years, 9.0% over 5 years and 7.9% over 10 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
Free cash flow has compounded -20.4% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Forward indicators: a backlog worth 0% of annual revenue and deferred revenue down 16%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (1.3x, 1.5% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 10, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders own a modest 2.2%, and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insider trading is two-way: 4 purchases and 2 sales over the past year, net $1.1M bought.
It returns 15.5% a year to shareholders (15.5% in buybacks).
The share count has shrunk 4.5% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
Short interest is elevated at 15.7% of the float, 5.7 days to cover.
people: With about 8,281 employees, each generates about $458K of revenue, 1.3x the Industrials median, and revenue has grown 6.9% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $11K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $2.8M (6x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (2/10, lower is better).
